If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.

If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon (8–14 days), reduce forecast by 1–2% to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) in the last 3 days, apply a 0.5–1% downward adjustment to mid-horizon (8–14 days) forecasts to smooth volatility.

If sentiment is positive but forecasted price is rising sharply (slope >0.1% per day), reduce forecast by 1–2% for late horizon (15–30 days) to prevent over-leverage.

If sentiment is negative but forecasted price is falling sharply (slope < -0.1% per day), increase forecast by 1–2% for late horizon (15–30 days) to offset bearish momentum.
